name: Komering
confidence_why: The only Komering phonology that treats suprasegmentals, Saleh et al. 1984, names open juncture as the language's sole suprasegmental phoneme and gives no stress placement, and Abdurrahman and Yallop 1979 say nothing about stress at all, so the record's 'undetermined' rests on a single first-hand source with nothing contradicting it.

catalog_quote: 3.3 Fonem Suprasegmental. Di dalam bahasa Komering terdapat hanya satu fonem suprasegmental, yaitu fonem jeda terbuka atau jeda tambah. Kemampuan fonem jeda terbuka mengubah arti seperti yang ditunjukkan dalam pasangan minimal di bawah ini. a) /ŋarokop/ 'diam' /ŋa + rokop/ 'bibi diam' b) /sambolih/ 'sembelih' sam + bolih/ 'Sam yang cerewat' c) /bujaŋuluŋ/ 'babi' /bujaŋ + uluŋ/ 'bujang tua' ... [p. 206:] Dalam bahasa Komering hanya ada satu fonem suprasegmental, yakni fonem jeda terbuka atau ope juncture, misalnya: /ŋarokop/ 'diam' /ŋa + rokop/ 'bibi diam. ... [sec. 4.1, p. 27:] Morfem kata kerja bahasa Komering mempunyai wujud yang terdiri dari fonem segmental saja. Dalam bahasa ini tidak ada morfem kata kerja yang mempunyai wujud fonem suprasegmental atau prosodi.

new_statements.translation: 3.3 Suprasegmental phonemes. In Komering there is only one suprasegmental phoneme, namely open juncture (plus juncture). The ability of open juncture to change meaning is shown by the minimal pairs below: /ŋarokop/ 'be silent' vs /ŋa + rokop/ 'aunt is silent' ... [p. 206:] In Komering there is only one suprasegmental phoneme, namely open juncture ... [4.1:] Komering verb morphemes consist of segmental phonemes only. In this language there is no verb morpheme whose shape involves a suprasegmental phoneme or prosody.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The source treats stress (and tone) as non-phonemic in Komering: the only contrastive suprasegmental is open juncture. It does NOT say on which syllable word stress falls; no placement rule is recoverable from any source opened.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the phoneme inventory (word-level contrast), based on Komering Ulu dialects (Buay Madang, Cempaka, Belitang; Martapura-Simpang noted for vowel differences). Abdurrahman & Yallop 1979 (Adumanis, Komering Ulu), the only dedicated phonology paper, is silent on stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Abdurrahman & Yallop 1979 describe Komering Ulu, Adumanis village dialect; Saleh et al. 1984 base their phonology on Komering Ulu dialects (Buay Madang, Cempaka, Belitang; Martapura-Simpang differs in vowels and /r/). The Kayu Agung books (Dunggio et al. 1984; Gani et al. 1986) describe Kayu Agung, formerly ISO [vky] (Glottolog kayu1244, bookkeeping), merged into Komering [kge] in 2008; Anderbeck 2007 treats Kayu Agung Asli vs Kayu Agung (Pendatang) as distinct Lampungic lects, so a Kayu Agung statement would need a dialect flag.

sources.note: Bab III Fonologi 3.3 (pp. 20-21) and Bab VI p. 206: Komering has only ONE suprasegmental phoneme, open juncture (jeda terbuka); 4.1: verb morphemes consist of segmental phonemes only, none has a suprasegmental/prosodic shape. I.e. stress is treated as non-phonemic, but NO statement of where stress falls.
